text:
Maya: Heads-up — got an enterprise SQ asking for quick answers about logging and PII. They want: encryption at rest, KMS/subprocessor list, log redaction controls, and who approves access. Can someone drop a short copy-pasteable reply?
Trent: I can do a first pass. Are they asking for streaming logs or persisted audit logs?
Maya: Mostly persisted audit logs + request traces. They want assurance that no raw PII ends up in retained logs.
Sam: Short answer: logs are encrypted at rest with customer-segmented KMS keys for Dedicated/Private, and access to logs is role-gated with audit trails. For hosted tenants we rotate service KMS keys regularly and subprocessors are listed in our compliance pack.
Jules: Add a note about redaction: we use prefix-based KV masking + regex-based redaction in the ingestion pipeline. Typical rule example: `s/(\\b\\d{3}[-.]?\\d{2}[-.]?\\d{4}\\b)/[REDACTED_SSN]/g` and we scrub long substrings that look like tokens.
Maya: Nice. Customer asked for the exact subprocessors for KMS and log storage — can we point them to the published list and also share the contract-facing subproc list on request?
Trent: Yes — point them to https://redwood.example.com/compliance/subprocessors and say we can provide an executed subproc list under NDA for procurement.
Sam: For SOC2/ISO question: we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 docs in the compliance portal. We also track controls for logging redaction in the SOC2 evidence repo. Add: we do periodic review of redaction rules after major model or API changes.
Maya: Who needs to approve a one-off log access request for debugging customer incidents? They asked about the approval process.
Jules: Standard flow: engineer files request in the access request tool, manager + security approver sign off (currently sec-approvers group), access is time-bound and audited. We revoke keys and record TTL.
Trent: I'll paste the short copy for procurement: "Redwood encrypts logs at rest and in transit, maintains a published subprocessor list, enforces role-based access with manager+security approval for ad-hoc access, and applies automated redaction and regex masking to prevent PII retention. Full compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO) are available in the compliance portal; executed subprocessor agreements can be shared under NDA."
Maya: Perfect. Quick extra ask: they want an example of the redaction config snippet. Can we include one-liner they can paste?
Jules: Use this minimal snippet: ```regex: - pattern: "\\b\\d{3}[-.]?\\d{2}[-.]?\\d{4}\\b"   replace: "[REDACTED_SSN]"```
Sam: Also add: we have automatic entropy/token detectors to catch long secrets and we block retention pre-storage.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll send this back. If procurement asks for the contract subproc list, ping legal and security.
